This is a fresh announcement opening a new object, a covenant not yet named, rather than pointing anaphorically back to days already announced the way the proverb material just closed does; the person shift to first person at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte) and the incipit's own recurrence elsewhere in the book corroborate the fresh announcement rather than driving it alone. boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens the cosmic-guarantee unit, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה נֹתֵ֥ן שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ לְא֣וֹר יוֹמָ֔ם חֻקֹּ֛ת יָרֵ֥חַ וְכוֹכָבִ֖ים לְא֣וֹר לָ֑יְלָה רֹגַ֤ע הַיָּם֙ וַיֶּהֱמ֣וּ גַלָּ֔יו יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.31.35, byte), matching “Yahweh, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea, so that its waves roar— Yahweh of Armies is his name, says:” (web:Jer.31.35) — the fixed order of sun, moon, stars, and sea, named as warrant for what follows; this verse itself carries a paseq. A second koh-amar repeats the identical if-then oath structure with a different cosmic image, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם יִמַּ֤דּוּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה וְיֵחָקְר֥וּ מֽוֹסְדֵי אֶ֖רֶץ לְמָ֑טָּה גַּם אֲנִ֞י אֶמְאַ֨ס בְּכָל זֶ֧רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַֽל כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.31.37, byte), matching “Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.31.37) “If heaven above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath, then I will also cast off all the offspring of Israel for all that they have done,” says Yahweh. boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a dated word-event header, הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.1, byte), matching “This is the word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh” (web:Jer.32.1). A ketiv/qere note sits inside the date phrase itself: ketiv בשנת against qere בַּשָּׁנָה֙ (oshb:Jer.32.1, WLC, single-witness). The header closes on a second regnal count, הִ֧יא הַשָּׁנָ֛ה שְׁמֹנֶֽה עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּֽר (oshb:Jer.32.1, byte), matching “which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar” (web:Jer.32.1), naming the king in the resh-family spelling the bytes carry here. A circumstantial notice follows without a break, הָיָ֤ה כָלוּא֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.2, byte), matching “Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard” (web:Jer.32.2). A relative clause then names who confined him, אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּלָא֔וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.32.3, byte), matching “For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying,” (web:Jer.32.3), and the charge Zedekiah brings is itself a question quoting, at one remove, Jeremiah’s own earlier announcement against the city: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֜ן אֶת הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את (oshb:Jer.32.3, byte), matching “Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will take it;” (web:Jer.32.3), continuing through the king’s own capture, “and Zedekiah king of Judah won’t escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but will surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon” (web:Jer.32.4). It closes on Yahweh’s own sentence as Zedekiah’s charge reports it, “though you fight with the Chaldeans, you will not prosper” (web:Jer.32.5). Nothing across these five verses marks a change of speaker away from the narrator’s own third-person report of Jeremiah and Zedekiah; that shift comes only at the next verse, where the account turns to Jeremiah’s own first-person voice, “Jeremiah said,” (web:Jer.32.6), and this row stops short of it.

boundary_rationale: The narration turns to Jeremiah’s own first-person voice, וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte tier), matching “Jeremiah said, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Jer.32.6) — the command phase of the sign that follows opens at once with a named relative arriving, “Behold, Hanamel the son of Shallum your uncle will come to you, saying,” (web:Jer.32.7), sent to buy “my field that is in Anathoth” (web:Jer.32.7). The performance follows without any further command, וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לַי חֲנַמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן דֹּדִ֜י כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל חֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָה֒ (oshb:Jer.32.8, byte), matching “So Hanamel my uncle’s son came to me in the court of the guard according to Yahweh’s word” (web:Jer.32.8) — a WEB paragraph break falls inside this very verse, between the arrival and Jeremiah’s own closing note that he then knew the word was Yahweh’s, a modern formatting fold rather than any textual seam. The purchase itself, the weighing of silver, the sealing and witnessing of the deed, and its delivery to Baruch all continue this same first-person report through וָֽאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת בָּר֔וּךְ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.13, byte), matching “I commanded Baruch before them, saying,” (web:Jer.32.13), which opens the interpretation phase: כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.32.14, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says:” (web:Jer.32.14), charging that the deeds be preserved “that they may last many days” (web:Jer.32.14), and closing on the reason given for the whole sign, כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.32.15, byte), matching “For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says: ‘Houses and fields and vineyards will yet again be bought in this land.’” (web:Jer.32.15). Command, performance, and interpretation are held here as one unit because no addressee shift, frame-owner change, or discourse imperative interrupts them anywhere in between; the seam comes only where Jeremiah turns from reporting the purchase to reporting his own prayer, “I prayed to Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.32.16), and this row is bounded there.

boundary_rationale: A prayer-frame verb opens the unit on its own, וָאֶתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.32.16, byte), matching “I prayed to Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.32.16), turning Jeremiah’s own report from narrating the purchase to addressing God directly. The address opens with a vocative divine title, אֲהָהּ֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Jer.32.17, byte), matching “Ah Lord Yahweh! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power” (web:Jer.32.17), and states as its own premise “There is nothing too hard for you” (web:Jer.32.17). Praise of Yahweh’s power and justice continues through a recital of the exodus, the gift of the land, and Israel’s own disobedience, unbroken by any new addressee, until a fresh “Behold” turns the address to the present siege, הִנֵּ֣ה הַסֹּלְל֗וֹת בָּ֣אוּ הָעִיר֮ (oshb:Jer.32.24, byte), matching “Behold, siege ramps have been built against the city to take it” (web:Jer.32.24). It closes on the tension between the command just carried out and the circumstance surrounding it, וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ אֵלַי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.25, byte), matching “You have said to me, Lord Yahweh, ‘Buy the field for money, and call witnesses;’” (web:Jer.32.25), “whereas the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans” (web:Jer.32.25). This whole address to God is held as one unit because it is never interrupted by a new addressee or a change of speaker — it moves from praise through historical recital to present crisis and an unresolved question without ever leaving Jeremiah’s own voice directed at Yahweh; the next word-event formula reopens address as Yahweh’s own reply, “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.32.26), and this row ends just short of it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Typing this span as a hymn of praise rather than a lament was considered, since verses 17 through 23 are sustained creation-and-exodus praise close in shape to the doxologies elsewhere in the book; it is held here as a personal address to God running to an unresolved question instead, since the unit does not close on praise but on Jeremiah’s own bewildered complaint at the gap between command and circumstance, the same shape the book’s confessions take even though this address carries none of their persecution content.
